newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds weakened towards the close after flirting with higher levels in early afternoon, as profit-taking dominated late business, traders said.
"We really saw some profit-taking towards the end and the U.S. didn't perform particularly well," one trader said.
A certain degree of nervousness restricted volumes, but the market's main problem was the scarcity of buyers.
Traders were split as to the future direction of the market, but the consensus seemed to be drifting towards the bearish side, at least in the short-term.
"I think we could see quite a further fall tomorrow. We really need to bottom out," he said.

Investors, reasoned some traders, were unlikely to return to, for example, the ten year benchmark paper until yields headed up to 5.60 percent. On Thursday, the 5.75 percent 2007s closed at 101.50/58 for a bid yield of 5.54 percent.
Traders said the day had no strong themes, although most noted a slightly better buying of shorter maturities.
"It's a bit of a bull-bear situation at the moment," one trader said.
One cloud on the horizon for shorter prices was the prospect of rising money market rates as the weakness of the guilder against the mark persisted. The mark made further advances on Thursday.
